about.text: Galalith is a synthetic plastic material manufactured by the interaction of casein and formaldehyde. The commercial name is derived from the Ancient Greek words gala and lithos. It is odourless, hard, resists humidity to a certain degree, is antistatic, also an electrical insulator and virtually nonflammable. It was produced under a plethora of other commercial names such as aladdinite, Casolith and lactoloid.

how.text: Casein is first formed into rods, tubes or sheets, and only then hardened: the shaped piece soaks in a formaldehyde bath that cross-links the protein into an insoluble, horn-like thermoset. Because the bath works from the outside in, the hardening is the long step.

steps.note: Dry casein powder is mixed with colourants.
Pressed into bars and re-extruded, then the bars are pressed into blocks.

steps.name: harden
steps.note: In a formaldehyde bath of about 5 % (formalin), weeks to months and up to a year for 25 mm thickness.
Slowly, to avoid cracking and warping.
